title: saving an inputmap with ProjectSettings.save() and EditorInterface.restart_editor()
body: ### Tested versions tested in godot 4.6.3 only ### System information Godot v4.6.3.stable - Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS 24.04 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (TGL GT2) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1135G7 @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) - 15.35 GiB memory ### Issue description I'm building an `EditorPlugin` that writes custom key/gamepad bindings into `ProjectSettings` (`input/*` actions) so a game repo ships with a working default control scheme out of the box. The bindings themselves work and correctly appear under **Project Settings > Input Map** — but only after a *manual* editor restart. To automate that restart from `_enable_plugin()` / `_disable_plugin()`, I call `EditorInterface.restart_editor()`. This does not behave the same as a manual restart, and produces three different outcomes depending on whether any file is unsaved at the moment the plugin is toggled: | Case | State when toggled | Result | |---|---|---| | 1 | Any file unsaved (scene or script) | Works exactly as intended — bindings apply, restart completes, and the "enabled" checkbox in **Project Settings > Plugins** correctly reflects the new state. | | 2 | All files saved, toggling plugin **off** | Plugin logic runs, but the "enabled" checkbox does **not** update, and the editor **crashes** instead of restarting. | | 3 | All files saved, toggling plugin **on** | Plugin logic runs and the editor restarts without crashing, but the "enabled" checkbox still does **not** reflect the new state. | So the only combination that behaves correctly end-to-end is when something happens to be unsaved at the moment `restart_editor()` fires — every fully saved state either fails to persist the plugin's own enabled/disabled flag or crashes. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create an `EditorPlugin` whose `_enable_plugin()` / `_disable_plugin()` write settings via `ProjectSettings.set_setting()`, call `ProjectSettings.save()`, then call `EditorInterface.restart_editor()`. 2. With no unsaved scenes or scripts open anywhere in the editor, enable the plugin from **Project Settings > Plugins**. The editor restarts, but the checkbox doesn't show as checked → **Case 3**. 3. With no unsaved scenes or scripts open, disable an already-enabled plugin the same way. The editor crashes instead of restarting → **Case 2**. 4. Repeat either toggle with an unsaved scene or script open elsewhere in the editor. Everything works correctly, including the checkbox state → **Case 1**. ```gdscript ## this script sets a defualt contol lay out based on the deveopler of fightvainia's contol scheme in a auto load ## fightvaina defualt contols witch are bad but work for testing # this script had some ai help and some jsut finding things online @tool extends EditorPlugin const dictionarykeys: Dictionary[StringName, Key] = { "frame by frame mode 2": KEY_F, "right 2": KEY_D, "left 2": KEY_A, "up 2": KEY_W, "down 2": KEY_S, "LP 2": KEY_K, "HP 2": KEY_O, "LK and jump 2": KEY_L, "HK and block 2": KEY_P, "menu 2": KEY_ESCAPE,} const dictionaryjoys: Dictionary[StringName, JoyButton] = { "frame by frame mode 2": JOY_BUTTON_BACK, "right 2": JOY_BUTTON_DPAD_RIGHT, "left 2": JOY_BUTTON_DPAD_LEFT, "up 2": JOY_BUTTON_DPAD_UP, "down 2": JOY_BUTTON_DPAD_DOWN, "LP 2": JOY_BUTTON_X, "HP 2": JOY_BUTTON_Y, "LK and jump 2": JOY_BUTTON_A, "HK and block 2": JOY_BUTTON_B, "menu 2": JOY_BUTTON_START,} ## this dictoary was made with ai as i was unsure how to use the right values for the joy axis const dictionaryjoyaxis: Dictionary[StringName, Dictionary] = { "right 2": {"axis": JOY_AXIS_LEFT_X, "value": 1.0}, "left 2": {"axis": JOY_AXIS_LEFT_X, "value": -1.0}, "down 2": {"axis": JOY_AXIS_LEFT_Y, "value": 1.0}, "up 2": {"axis": JOY_AXIS_LEFT_Y, "value": -1.0},} func _enable_plugin() -> void: set_up(true) ProjectSettings.save() EditorInterface.restart_editor() func _disable_plugin() -> void: set_up(false) ProjectSettings.save() EditorInterface.restart_editor() func set_up(turn_on: bool): # clean up of inputs to prevent multiple copys of the same key for i in dictionarykeys: set_up_helper(i,dictionarykeys[i], true, 0) for i in dictionaryjoys: set_up_helper(i,dictionaryjoys[i], true, 1) for i in dictionaryjoyaxis: set_up_helper(i,dictionaryjoyaxis[i], true, 2) if turn_on: for i in dictionarykeys: set_up_helper(i,dictionarykeys[i], false, 0) for i in dictionaryjoys: set_up_helper(i,dictionaryjoys[i], false, 1) for i in dictionaryjoyaxis: set_up_helper(i,dictionaryjoyaxis[i], false, 2) func set_up_helper(input_name: StringName, input, remove: bool = false, thing: int = 0): input_name = "input/"+input_name # set the input name var event if thing == 0: event = InputEventKey.new() # the input event / key event.physical_keycode = input elif thing == 1: event = InputEventJoypadButton.new() # the input event / key event.button_index = input event.device = -1 elif thing == 2: event = InputEventJoypadMotion.new() event.axis = input["axis"] event.axis_value = input["value"] event.device = -1 #append so w can have more then 1 input var action = ProjectSettings.get(input_name) if action: action.events.append(event) # the input events / key else: action = { deadzone = 0.2, events = [event] } if remove: ProjectSettings.set(input_name, null) else: ProjectSettings.set(input_name, action) ``` the diolog box i mentioned ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) i assume n/a as its a single script with a plugin config but i included one anyway [mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30602265/mrp.zip)
